newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch "unaware" of deal to name French ECB chief.
newsitem.headline: Dutch "unaware" of deal to name French ECB chief.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Thursday he was unaware of a Franco-German deal to appoint a Frenchman as first head of the European Central Bank, adding that Dutchman Wim Duisenberg remained the best candidate.
"Neither I nor (foreign) minister (Hans) van Mierlo know of any such agreement," Dutch news agency ANP quoted Kok as saying.

Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg is due to take over as president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), forerunner of the European Central Bank (ECB), in July and had been widely expected to become the first president of the ECB.
But in December French President Jacques Chirac said that Duisenberg would not automatically head the ECB.

In a recent magazine interview Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli said that when it was decided to locate the ECB in Frankfurt there was an "unspoken commitment" by Germany that the bank's first president would be French.

German magazine Wirtschaftswoche said this week that Frenchman Jacques Delors was an ideal candidate to head the ECB, adding that the choice of candidate would be made by France since Germany had won its fight to bring the bank to Frankfurt.
The Dutch prime minister, speaking after talks with visiting Flemish leader Luc van den Brande, said the Netherlands still stood squarely behind Duisenberg's candidacy.
"Quality always shines through and Mr Duisenberg is an illustration of that. He will prove himself to be the best candidate, even to the French," ANP quoted Kok as saying.
